title: Steering Vectors for Deceptive Alignment Detection

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Deceptive alignment is a central AI safety concern with no scalable detection method. If concept vectors can flag deceptive internal states, this provides an early-warning system for one of the most dangerous alignment failure modes. Maximum impact chain clarity.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires generating known deceptive-vs-honest model outputs to create contrastive pairs, which itself requires sophisticated prompting or fine-tuning. Extracting concept vectors and validating them against downstream unsafe behavior is technically demanding. Beginners would need heavy mentorship.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple open-ended components: generating deceptive behavior data, extracting concept vectors, validating predictive power on held-out prompts. The deceptive behavior generation alone is an open research problem.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
